description: HardGrind No-OP is a singleplayer discipline mod for Fabric 1.21.9. It removes every shortcut that could ruin your grind — no /op, no /gamemode, no cheating. Even in singleplayer, you play by the same rules as on a real public survival server.

releases.notes:
Everything since 1.1.0. Download the jar for your Minecraft version and install it with Fabric API for that version.

| Minecraft | Jar | Java |
|---|---|---|
| 1.21.9 | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+1.21.9.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.10 | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+1.21.10.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.11 | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+1.21.11.jar` | 21 |
| 26.1 - 26.1.2 | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+26.1.2.jar` | 25 |
| 26.2 | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+26.2.jar` | 25 |
| 26.3 and newer | `hardgrind-noop-1.9.1+26.3.jar` | 25 |

## Minecraft versions
- One jar per version now: 1.21.9, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1 to 26.1.2, 26.2, and 26.3 and newer (the 26.3 jar keeps loading on later versions). 1.1.0 was 1.21.9 only.

## OP and Survival
- OP is removed at the source: every player's permissions are always the lowest level, whether they're in `ops.json`, in a singleplayer world with cheats on, or opened to LAN with "Allow Cheats".
- That blocks every op command (`/gamemode`, `/give`, `/tp`, `/gamerule`, `/op`, ...) and the F3+F4 / F3+N game mode switcher.
- The server console and datapack functions keep their permissions.
- Survival is enforced: players in any other mode are put back on the next tick. In Hardcore, dead players are left in Spectator.

## Difficulty and gamerules
- **New: the difficulty is locked** at what the world had when HardGrind first saw it. The Difficulty button no longer lets you switch to Peaceful mid-fight.
- **More gamerules are locked:** keepInventory, doDaylightCycle, doWeatherCycle, doMobSpawning, spawnMonsters (1.21.11+), mobGriefing, naturalRegeneration, doImmediateRespawn, randomTickSpeed, playersSleepingPercentage, fallDamage, fireDamage, drowningDamage and freezeDamage.
- Changes (for example from editing `level.dat`) are reverted within 5 seconds.
- **Fixed:** 1.1.x only recorded real gamerule values in a development environment. They're recorded properly now.

## New: run log and milestones
- `/hardgrind log` shows the day, play time, deaths, mob kills, a milestone timeline and any notes.
- The big steps of a run are announced and stamped with the day and play time: Stone Age, Acquire Hardware, Diamonds!, the Nether, blaze rods, Eye Spy, the End, the dragon, elytra, ancient debris, full netherite, a full beacon.
- Permanent notes record anything outside HardGrind's control: play without the mod, a crash or force-quit, or anything caught. Players are told on join.
- One line sums up the run when you join, e.g. `HardGrind · Day 12 · Run: Ironman · clean · watching since Day 1`.

## New: locking a world (`/hardgrind lock confirm`)
- **The world won't open without HardGrind.** A small datapack points at a sound only HardGrind adds, so without the mod Minecraft stops with "data pack validation failed".
- **Safe Mode is caught:** the only way in without the mod switches the lock off, and HardGrind notices when it's back.
- **Backup if the datapack runs without the mod:** everyone is frozen; Creative/Spectator, changed gamerules and a changed difficulty are reverted and recorded; and vanilla's "Lock Difficulty" is set.
- **Save-scum guard:** restored backups and old copies behind the latest save are caught, and only that copy pays for it. A dead world stays dead even if you restore a backup.
- **Force-quit protection:** locked worlds save every 2 minutes, and right away when someone dies or drops to 3 hearts.
- **Cheat-mod guard:** a locked world won't load with X-ray mods, Baritone or hacked clients (Wurst, Meteor, Aristois, BleachHack, LiquidBounce, ThunderHack). Minimaps, inventory tweaks and recipe viewers are fine.
- **Tampering checks:** the datapack deleted, switched off or edited, `hardgrind.marker` deleted, a changed difficulty, a rollback, or play time without the datapack all go into the run log.
- Updating HardGrind never counts as tampering: packs written by older versions are recognised.
- `/hardgrind unlock confirm` takes the lock out again, with a permanent note.

## New: ironman (`/hardgrind ironman confirm`)

releases.notes:
HardGrind No-OP 1.1.0 (Universal Build – No LAN)

This update makes HardGrind No-OP fully universal — working both in singleplayer and on Fabric servers.
It keeps your survival discipline untouched while improving stability and removing unnecessary client hooks.

Core changes

Unified client + server build (one .jar for both)

Replaced GameRules.getRule(String) calls with stable field-based reflection
→ Fixes build issues on Minecraft 1.21.9 and future-proofs gamerule checks

Removed Open-to-LAN mixin for cleaner singleplayer integration

Improved hardcore detection and gamemode enforcement

Hardened gamerule firewall — restores protected rules every 5 seconds

Blocked command list expanded:
/op, /deop, /gamemode, /give, /tp, /summon, /effect, /xp, /enchant, /locate, /gamerule

Added automatic policy marker file (hardgrind.marker) for gamerule persistence

Switched project language to English, added MIT License and README

Technical

Minecraft 1.21.9

Fabric Loader 0.17.2+

Fabric API 0.134.0+

Java 21 required

Next focus

Version range support for 1.20 → 1.21.x

Optional server-side marker sync
